name: AI News
blurb: Daily AI news from the publishers who broke it, split into headline coverage of the field and vendor announcements from the companies building it. Every story links to the original source, and any claim quoted in our coverage is cross-referenced against the laws, lawsuits, companies, tools, papers, and people already tracked in this atlas.

domains.name: AI Headline News
domains.blurb: The day's most consequential AI stories across law, policy, research, safety, and society, curated from 34 vetted feeds. Each item carries the original publisher link and a note on how it connects to the bills, cases, and frameworks tracked elsewhere on this site.

domains.name: AI Vendor News
domains.blurb: Product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements from the AI vendors themselves. Each item links to the vendor's original announcement and cross-references the company's profile in our AI Companies directory where one exists.

domains.name: This Week in AI
domains.blurb: A weekly record of what moved in AI policy and litigation, permalinked by ISO week.

domains.name: AI Historical Timeline
domains.blurb: From the 1940s to the present: Turing, the perceptron, expert systems, backpropagation, deep learning, AlexNet, transformers, and what followed.

reading.body:
Daily AI news from 34 vetted sources reaches 403 pages of headline coverage, while vendor announcements occupy a single page, suggesting that external reporting on AI development vastly outpaces the announcements companies make themselves.

The disparity reflects the reality that policy, law, research, and societal consequence now move faster in AI than corporate marketing can address. Regulatory actions, safety findings, litigation outcomes, and competitive breakthroughs generate news streams that require constant curation. A vendor announcement—a model release or pricing change—is discrete and infrequent. A court ruling or legislative proposal affects the entire industry at once.

For tracking how compute and power constrain AI, this imbalance matters. Infrastructure decisions by individual companies do not generate daily news. Grid capacity, data center permits, power supply agreements, and chip allocation are backend decisions that surface only when they fail or become politically visible. The 403-page headline feed will capture those moments. The vendor news section will not.

The cross-referencing across laws, lawsuits, companies, and people means the site treats these stories not as isolated events but as evidence within a connected system. A news story links to the regulatory or corporate context it affects. That approach works only when the volume of news is high and the underlying network of constraints is mapped. Here, that volume exists on the headline side, where it can be continuously updated and connected to the rest of the atlas.
